Acoustics. Nature is our core journal, of course…

After all, a few acoustics papers have appeared in Nature over the past hundred-odd years. Does that count…


Acoustics spans an enormous range and not many people work in it, so impact factors are pitifully low and there aren’t many journals to publish in. Here’s a summary:


  • The broadest coverage, general acoustics:
    • JASA (US), Acta (Europe) and Applied Acoustics (UK);
    • and the recently launched Acoustics (a name as simple as it is commanding), edited by Professor Jian Kang of UCL;
  • Leaning toward mechanical vibration: JSV;
  • Leaning toward speech, audio and signal processing: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing;
  • Leaning toward aerospace: AIAA;
  • Leaning toward numerical methods: Journal of Computational Acoustics.

Those are the core journals. Then there are the so-called “non-core” ones, such as

  • Noise Control Engineering Journal
  • Archives of Acoustics
  • Building Acoustics


There are other journals with “acoustics” in their names, but they go beyond a discussion of core journals.


To learn more about this arcane art, come and browse my acoustics column:

Tech you can hear: acoustics

Addendum (thanks to @wgdd):

A journal with a high impact factor: Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing. Publish your acoustics papers there and you won’t have to worry about impact factors.
